title: A zero neighbourhood for an etale section killed by inverse image
statement: Let $X,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $V\to X$ an etale object [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], $a:T\to V$, and $p:T\to X$ satisfy $a$ followed by the structure map of $V$ equals $p$. Let $F$ be an abelian etale sheaf on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] and let $H$ be any left adjoint to $p_*$, with its supplied adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For $s\in F(V)$ assume its image under the unit $F(V)\to H(F)(V\times_X T)$ followed by restriction along $(a,\mathrm{id}_T):T\to V\times_X T$ is zero. There exists an open subset $U\subseteq V$ containing $a(T)$ such that the restriction of $s$ to the etale object $U\to V\to X$ is zero.

source.place: Definition 59.29.6 (filtered-colimit stalks) in Tag 03PN; Lemma 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback) (3), with unit-germ compatibility

proof.text: For any geometric point of V, a zero germ of s is represented by an etale neighbourhood on which s restricts to zero. This is the filtered-colimit description of the stalk. The neighbourhood morphism is etale, hence open. It covers its image, and separatedness of F makes s zero on that image. Take U to be the union of all opens on which s is zero; separatedness on this covering makes s zero on U.

For a point t of T choose a geometric point over t. The stalk-of-pullback isomorphism, its unit-germ compatibility, and naturality of germs under restriction identify the germ of the canonical unit/restriction section with the germ of s at its image in V. The assumed zero section therefore gives a zero germ, so a(t) lies in U. Uniqueness of left adjoints to p_* identifies the supplied H with the standard inverse image and carries its unit to the supplied unit. This justifies the same calculation for any hH.

Thus the image of a lies in U and restriction of s to U is zero, as required. For empty T its image is empty; U may be empty. For s=0 one can take U=V. There is no affine or inverse-limit hypothesis in this statement.

proof_origin.place: Zero-germ argument, expanded by descent from an etale neighbourhood to its open image and the pullback stalk isomorphism
